title: Redis: strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets and streams

videos.script: Redis is often used as a box of strings. {{box}} Read a value, change it in the application, write it back. Two workers doing that at once lose updates. In this lesson they lose almost half. {{race}} The fix is to let the server make the change. Redis runs one command at a time, so a command that reads and writes cannot be interrupted. {{one-thread}} Every structure in this lesson is a set of commands like that. A string becomes a stock counter, or a lock that only one worker can take. {{strings}} A hash holds a product as fields, so a sale changes the stock and nothing else. {{hash}} A list keeps order, a set refuses duplicates, and a sorted set keeps the best sellers ranked on every sale. {{ranking}} Then streams. A list used as a queue deletes a job the moment a worker takes it. A stream keeps it, and remembers who took it and never said it was done. {{stream}} You will crash a worker on purpose, find the orders it was holding, and hand them to another one. {{claim}}
